messages:
alex: Heads up — ACME (acct 8347) reports big latency spikes and 5xxs last night. They say traces show requests bouncing regions (eu-west -> us-west) on retries. I can repro in logs: trace 2745a; sample below. Anyone seen SDK cause region changes across retries?
maria: @alex can you paste the log lines and the SDK version? Also did they set a preferred_region or use default routing policy?
alex: Log snippet:
```
[2026-02-23T03:12:01Z] req=2745a status=500 route=eu-west-1 attempt=1 host=eu1.redwood.net
[2026-02-23T03:12:02Z] req=2745a status=200 route=us-west-2 attempt=2 host=usw2.redwood.net latency=1.2s
x-region-hint: eu-west-1
```
SDK v0.9.1, default routing. They have custom timeout 800ms and hedged requests enabled.
sanjay: Hmm — hedged requests + aggressive timeout could trigger fallback to nearest available region. But SDK shouldn't hop regions mid-request. @tasha can you check routing logs? :eyes: 
tasha: Pulling router trace for req=2745a — shows initial route assigned eu-west-1, then client retry went to a different endpoint. Looks like SDK reset region header when re-resolving upstream after timeout.
leo: Which SDK language? Node/Go/py?
alex: Node (redwood-js) 0.9.1. Config they used:
```
new RedwoodClient({
  regionPolicy: "auto",
  timeouts: { request: 800 },
  hedgedRequests: { enabled: true, hedgeAfterMs: 200 },
})
```
jen: Repro steps from ACME: run a steady stream of requests with request timeout 800ms against eu endpoint. They see about 2% of requests routed to US with higher latency. Customer understandably upset (SLA hit). They filed support ticket 11823.
maria: Possible causes: (1) client selecting fallback region on retry because DNS pool returned different IPs for global LB, (2) SDK re-lookup when hedged triggers and picks other host, (3) router fallback policy when capacity low. We need to know if request pinning header is sent on retries.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy to routing-service/2026-02-22T21:40: applied
sanjay: Quick check — in Node SDK versions <0.9.3 we had bug where `x-redwood-region` header wasn't preserved across internal retry. That could explain it. Maria did we patch already?
maria: There's an open PR: preserve-region-on-retry. Not in production yet.
tasha: Repro in-house: ran node SDK 0.9.1 with hedgedRequests and `network=simulated` — observed routing bounce. Steps:
1) start local router with eu,us endpoints
2) set request timeout 800ms, hedgeAfter 200ms
3) simulate eu backend delay 600ms on first attempt
Result: first attempt hits eu, second hedged attempt goes to us host because header missing.
alex: Customer wants immediate mitigation. Options: (a) advise them to set `hedgedRequests.enabled=false` or increase timeout, (b) patch SDK and ask them to upgrade to 0.9.4 canary, (c) server-side enforce `pin-region` policy for pinned customers.
maria: Support suggestion message to customer:
"temporary workaround: set `hedgedRequests.enabled=false` or set `regionPolicy: 'prefer_local'` and bump request timeout to 1500ms. We're rolling a fix to the Node SDK to preserve region headers across retries."
sanjay: Created internal ticket INF-4521 to backport patch to 0.9.x and roll canary. Assign @leo to coordinate canary.
leo: Will run canary this afternoon. Also adding router-side guard: when request has `x-redwood-region` and is pinned, ignore region changes on retries for next 2 attempts.
jen: I'll update ticket and draft customer reply. Also include repro snippet curl:
```
for i in {1..100}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.net/v1/generate; done
```
and monitor `route` in logs.
alex: Thanks. Keeping this thread for coordination. Ping me if canary shows any regressions.
maria: FYI billing bot flagged sudden cross-region egress for account 8347 — @support please include cost note in customer reply.
billing-bot: alert: acct 8347 cross-region egress spike detected (estimate +$120 last 24h)
tasha: Noted. I'll add cost mitigation option: use `regionPolicy: 'strict'` to avoid cross-region routing until fix.
sanjay: Thanks team. Will follow up once INF-4521 is deployed.
